summary: <cite index="10-3,11-3">US stocks plunged on Thursday as a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections sparked fears over AI regulation and data center growth, triggering a massive selloff in semiconductor and tech stocks that erased Wednesday's post-election rally.</cite> <cite index="11-6,13-6">The PHLX Semiconductor index plummeted 10%, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 5% and erasing $1.9 trillion in value, while the S&P 500 dropped nearly 4% and the Dow shed over 1,500 points.</cite> <cite index="10-5,10-6">Nvidia slid 9% and Qualcomm sank on weak outlooks, while Tesla and SpaceX each lost over 9%.</cite> <cite index="20-1,20-6,27-4">Crypto markets initially rebounded after the midterms, with Bitcoin reclaiming $80,000 and Ethereum topping $2,400, supported by the first November ETF inflows, though the rally cooled as stock selloff intensified.</cite> <cite index="4-7,4-10,5-1">The Fed held rates steady last week and upgraded its economic assessment from "solid" to "strong," though recent inflation data showed the PCE index rising 0.5% in September, the fastest since March.</cite> <cite index="29-4,29-7,29-9">On the earnings front, ConocoPhillips beat with $3.27 EPS on surging oil prices, while Cummins saw strong demand from AI data center power equipment driving a 13% revenue increase.</cite>

signals.title: Democrat midterm sweep triggers AI stock rout on regulation fears
signals.desc: Post-election Democratic control of Congress sparked massive selling in chip and AI stocks on fears of tighter regulation, with semiconductors down 10% in worst day since April 2025 tariff crisis.

signals.title: Nasdaq erases $1.9 trillion as tech selloff spreads beyond chips
signals.desc: Broad tech weakness overwhelmed markets with Nasdaq down 5%, S&P 500 off 4%, and mega-cap names like Nvidia (-9%), Tesla (-9%) leading declines as AI buildout concerns mount.

signals.title: Bitcoin falls 5.5% as crypto rally stalls at key resistance
signals.desc: Crypto reversed sharply after briefly topping $80,000, with Bitcoin dropping back to $76,500 range and Ethereum losing $2,400 level as stock market turmoil weighs on risk assets.

signals.title: Fed upgrades growth outlook to "strong" but holds rates amid sticky inflation
signals.desc: The Federal Reserve described economic activity as expanding at a "strong" pace versus prior "solid" assessment, while September PCE inflation accelerated to 0.5% monthly, complicating rate cut path.

signals.title: Oil producer earnings beat as energy prices surge on supply concerns
signals.desc: ConocoPhillips crushed estimates with $3.27 EPS as realized oil/gas prices jumped 32% year-over-year to $61.40 per barrel equivalent, reflecting tight supply conditions.

verdict: Risk-off dominates as political uncertainty around AI regulation triggers historic tech washout, overwhelming initial post-election optimism and crypto bounce.
